project: LadhaQuest — Africa-first recipe and cooking platform

research_status.ladhaquest_site: Direct crawl/fetch of https://www.ladhaquest.com did not return page content and public search results were unavailable; treat the current feature inventory as a proposed baseline to validate against the live product.
research_status.benchmark: Allrecipes is a mature community-led recipe platform with 51K+ original recipes, 7M+ ratings/reviews, 67M home cooks, editorial testing, videos, saved recipes, and strong community feedback loops. [page:1]
research_status.market_patterns: Leading recipe and meal-planning products converge on recipe discovery, saving/import, weekly meal calendars, serving scaling, aisle-sorted grocery lists, household sharing, and grocery delivery integration. [web:2][web:3][web:7][web:10]

positioning.vision: Become Africa's trusted kitchen operating system: discover, cook, plan, shop for, and share African and global food with locally relevant tools.
positioning.category: African-first food discovery, meal planning, and commerce platform

primary_users.need: Reliable local recipes, substitutes, budgeting, and family-sized planning
Authentic dishes, hard-to-find ingredients, cultural connection, and delivery options
Fast weekly plans, affordable shopping lists, and low-friction cooking
Publishing, audience growth, monetization, and recipe analytics
Demand insight, local ingredient sourcing, branded recipes, and customer acquisition

positioning.core_promise: Cook any African dish confidently with ingredients, measurements, substitutions, budgets, and shopping that work in your local market.

allrecipes.evidence: Allrecipes positions community feedback and home-cook contributions as central differentiators, with 51K+ recipes and 7M+ ratings/reviews. [page:1]
allrecipes.ladhaquest_counter: Build deeper African authenticity, local ingredient intelligence, market-level pricing, and mobile-first planning rather than competing only on recipe volume.

nytimes_cooking.evidence: NYT Cooking is frequently regarded as a benchmark for curated discovery and seamless cooking/planning workflows. [web:4]
nytimes_cooking.ladhaquest_counter: Combine credible African culinary curation with free, localized utility and creator-led regional expertise.

mealime_emeads.evidence: Meal-planning products commonly turn selected recipes into calendar plans and categorized shopping lists, with some integrating pickup or delivery. [web:3][web:10]
mealime_emeads.ladhaquest_counter: Localize plans to African staples, seasonal produce, household budgets, market vendors, and mobile-money-friendly checkout.

paprika_plan_to_eat.evidence: These tools emphasize importing recipes, scheduling them, scaling servings, and generating organized lists. [web:3][web:8][web:9]
paprika_plan_to_eat.ladhaquest_counter: Make import, family sharing, and offline cooking accessible on low-bandwidth African mobile networks.

supercook_whisk.evidence: Ingredient-based discovery and converting saved recipes into shopping lists are established user expectations. [web:7][web:13]
supercook_whisk.ladhaquest_counter: Create an Africa-specific pantry model including local grains, spices, leaves, tubers, flours, and market-available substitutions.

african_first_content.description: Treat African cuisines as primary, not a niche category.
must_have: Country, region, ethnic/community, occasion, and diaspora taxonomy
Verified recipes with chef, grandmother, food historian, and community contributor attribution
Regional variants and respectful naming conventions
Audio/video pronunciation for dish and ingredient names
Cultural context, history, serving customs, and dietary adaptations

local_ingredient_intelligence.description: Solve the biggest African cooking friction: finding, naming, and substituting ingredients locally.
must_have: Ingredient aliases across English, Swahili, Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Amharic, French, Portuguese, Arabic, and other priority languages
Local-market and supermarket availability by city/region
Seasonality and price indicators
Substitution engine for unavailable or expensive ingredients
Unit conversion for cups, grams, local measures, bunches, tins, and market portions
Pantry scan through photo, barcode, or manual entry

africa_native_commerce.description: Turn recipes into practical shopping outcomes without assuming a single retail model.
must_have: Grocery list grouped by market stall, supermarket aisle, and online basket
Multi-vendor comparison and delivery/pickup integrations
Mobile money, cards, cash-on-delivery, and split-household payment support
Budget-aware meal plans with cost ceilings
Local seller and farmer marketplace for specialty ingredients

creator_economy.description: Make African food creators, home cooks, chefs, and food historians owners of the platform's content advantage.
must_have: Creator profiles, verification, follower graphs, and recipe collections
Upload from video, photo, voice notes, URL, or structured form
AI-assisted recipe extraction with mandatory human review
Revenue share from ads, premium subscriptions, affiliate groceries, branded content, and recipe sales
Reputation system based on cooked photos, helpful substitutions, ratings, and repeat saves

mvp.goal: Prove that African cooks choose LadhaQuest for discovery, planning, and shopping.

ux_principles: Mobile-first and usable on low-end Android devices
Minimal data usage with offline-first recipes and lists
Large imagery, clear step navigation, and accessible typography
Local language and measurement support from day one
Never make users guess an unavailable ingredient: always offer a practical substitute
Respect cultural ownership and avoid genericizing African cuisines
Make the path from discovery to purchased ingredients under three taps

frontend: React Native or Expo mobile app
backend: Search service such as Meilisearch or Elasticsearch

ai_implementation_prompts_for_cursor.generate_data_model: Create a normalized PostgreSQL schema for the entities listed in technical_architecture.data_model_entities. Include UUID primary keys, soft deletes, audit timestamps, indexes for recipe search, and constraints for ingredient-unit conversions.
ai_implementation_prompts_for_cursor.build_recipe_schema: Create a TypeScript Zod schema for a recipe with title, slug, description, cuisine, country, region, servings, prepTime, cookTime, difficulty, ingredients, steps, equipment, nutrition, allergens, media, creator, source, license, and localization fields.
ai_implementation_prompts_for_cursor.build_grocery_engine: Implement a grocery-list service that merges ingredients across selected recipes, converts units, de-duplicates by normalized ingredient ID, groups items by aisle or market section, supports manual edits, and exports a shareable list.
ai_implementation_prompts_for_cursor.build_substitution_engine: Implement a substitution recommendation service that receives ingredient, country, dietary restrictions, budget, and available pantry items; return ranked alternatives with confidence, price impact, flavor-role match, and recipe adjustment notes.
ai_implementation_prompts_for_cursor.build_meal_planner: Implement a weekly meal planner API with household preferences, budget ceiling, dietary restrictions, recipe ratings, prep-ahead logic, leftovers reuse, and automatic grocery-list generation.
ai_implementation_prompts_for_cursor.build_offline_support: Implement offline-first caching for recipe pages, meal plans, and grocery lists using IndexedDB on web and SQLite/AsyncStorage on mobile; queue mutations and reconcile conflicts on reconnect.
ai_implementation_prompts_for_cursor.build_creator_portal: Create creator onboarding, recipe submission with AI extraction and human review, media upload, moderation queue, analytics dashboard, and payout-ready earnings model.
ai_implementation_prompts_for_cursor.build_search: Implement multilingual recipe search with typo tolerance, ingredient aliases, filters, semantic fallback, personalized ranking, and analytics events for query-to-recipe-click conversion.

activation: Complete first recipe view within 24 hours

launch_markets: Start with one or two high-engagement African markets plus a diaspora market; validate ingredient availability and delivery economics before scaling.
launch_motion: Recruit 100 trusted local creators and home cooks per launch city
Seed 500 high-quality, locally tested recipes across priority cuisines
Partner with market vendors, grocers, and delivery providers for shopping-list conversion
Run family and diaspora recipe-preservation campaigns
Offer creator revenue share and verification to build supply-side loyalty
Use short-form cooking video, WhatsApp sharing, and community challenges for acquisition

content_authenticity.risk: Incorrect or culturally insensitive recipes damage trust
content_authenticity.mitigation: Community review, chef verification, source attribution, and correction workflow

ingredient_availability.risk: Recommended ingredients may be unavailable or costly
ingredient_availability.mitigation: Location-aware inventory, substitution engine, and price-aware planning

low_connectivity.mitigation: Offline-first design, compressed media, and low-data mode

creator_supply.mitigation: Creator incentives, easy upload tools, editorial support, and revenue share

commerce_complexity.mitigation: Phase integrations by market and begin with list export, affiliate links, and selected partners

data_privacy.risk: Location, health, and payment data require strong protection
data_privacy.mitigation: Explicit consent, data minimization, encryption, regional compliance review, and granular permissions

recommended_build_order: Validate LadhaQuest's live feature inventory and user research in one launch market
Build recipe schema, search, recipe page, save, and offline mode
Ship meal planner, grocery list, substitution engine, and household sharing
Launch creator portal and community proof loops
Integrate one grocery or delivery partner and test list-to-order conversion
Add pantry recommendations, AI assistant, budget planning, and marketplace
